purpose: Sanitized structural reference for a separate local test account; no captured account or session values included.
offset_basis: Offsets refer to decoded complete frames; body offsets exclude 6-byte header.

evidence.capture_checks: Only frame lengths, bounds and terminator presence checked; captured values not output or persisted.

credential_shape_from_public_reference_o.wire_before_transport_encryption: LoginReq reads password as ASCII and passes it directly to BCrypt.Net.BCrypt.Verify.
credential_shape_from_public_reference_o.database_storage: Reference compares the received password string against a stored BCrypt hash.
credential_shape_from_public_reference_o.application_level_client_hash: No application-level password hashing step is shown in this reference parser/processor; do not infer that the transmitted field is a BCrypt hash.
credential_shape_from_public_reference_o.limits_note: Conservative limits leave a NUL inside each exact reference read window; these are not a claim about official client UI limits.

implementation_constraints: Use newly created local credentials and newly generated local user/session identifiers; never reuse captured account/session values.
Allocate exactly 326 response bytes and serialize integers explicitly little-endian; do not rely on host-native byte order.
Reference string CopyTo calls lack bounds checks. Enforce chosen local field limits and NUL termination explicitly.
Treat field names/semantics as reference evidence, not complete independent verification against the current proprietary server.
The unmapped 42..96 range contains modern fields or state not explained by this serializer; all-zero local values remain an untested experiment.
A structurally valid login success is not proof that the client can reach its lobby or play a match.
Reference credential handler prints request bytes and session token; do not carry those diagnostic logs into a new implementation.
Incoming credential slots may contain nonzero bytes after their NUL terminators; ignore that trailing buffer data rather than requiring zero padding. Outgoing local strings remain zero-padded.
